entries.note: Thin: MLE-bench medal cutoffs, the question's first named measure, are not assessed (retrieved but screened out; 40% key-paper recall), and the retrieval note claims no recall figure exists though a key list did.
Mostly abstract-level and second-hand (Cauchois and label-shift via other papers' summaries), so what is proved per method is only partly answered; boilerplate retrieval note.
Does not answer the subsampling-gap question and says so; the evidence is cross-study and mismatched (TabPFN, estimation simulation), and 'benchmark studies agree' rests on one source.
Correctly says nothing reports the experiment, but what remains is background on correlation effects; 50% key-paper recall, with SHAP and rule-ensemble foundations missed.
Finds no credal-vs-Wasserstein comparison; the Wasserstein evidence offered is tangential (large-N chance-constrained, single-paper citations) and the key credal paper was not retrieved.

Closing generalisation that agreement is high for simple numeric answers rests on one extractive-QA abstract, and 7.9% lenient-judge figure is loosely phrased; key-paper recall only 20% (Zheng, Survey).

Answers only the analytical-xgboost slice of the question (no random forests, no public-data stability) and frames itself around an improvement idea; Airfoil runtimes differ between tables (3.76 vs 6.72 s) unexplained.
Does not address its research question at all (admitted); the only experiment is two failed LLM ideas with suspicious zero variance, and the baseline row set is unknown.
